newsitem.title: USA: Federal-Mogul takes charges in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Federal-Mogul takes charges in Q4.

text.p: Federal-Mogul Corp said Thursday it took restructuring charges of $204 million pretax and a special charge of $60 million pretax against its fourth quarter earnings.

The $204 million pretax charges includes a write-off of $155 million of impaired goodwill and certain assets and other costs associated with the restructuring of international aftermarket operations, $13 million for employee severance costs, $22 million for facility closures and consolidations, and $14 million for other miscellaneous items.
Federal-Mogul said the restructuring will take most of 1997 to complete, and is expected to result in a reduction of about 2,900 people from its worldwide work force of 15,700.
It expects to use proceeds from the sale of its various international retail operations to pay down debt.

As a result of balance sheet and business unit reviews, it took a pretax special charge of $60 million, including $15 million for obsolete inventory, a $25 million increase in provisions for customer programs and receivables, $3 million write-down of fixed assets, $9 million in professional fees and employee severance, and $8 million in miscellaneous items.
"We have realigned our growth strategy behind our core competencies of engineering, manufacturing and distribution," Federal-Mogul chairman and chief executive officer Dick Snell said in a statement.

Included in the restructuring is the planned sale of 132 international retail operations in Australia, Chile, Ecuador, Panama, Puerto Rico, South Africa, and Venezuela, and the planned sale or restructuring of about 30 wholesale operations in 10 countries.

The firm plans to relocate product lines in its European manufacturing operations and cut the workforce, consolidate lighting products in Juarez, Mexico and close the Leiters Ford, Indiana manufacturing facility.

The company also plans to close two of Maysville, Kentucky's three central distribution warehouses; consolidate customer support functions in the U.S. and streamline administration and operational staff functions worldwide.
Included in that is the consolidation of European aftermarket management functions in Geneva, Switzerland into the Wiesbaden, Germany manufacturing headquarters.
